serverInfo.name: upper-route-planner-mcp
serverInfo.title: Upper Route Planner MCP by usefulapi

result.instructions: Tools for Upper Route Planner, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which stops are not on a route yet?"; "Create a route for tomorrow called North Loop and add these five addresses to it."; "Assign Jordan and Alex to route 18452, optimize it, and tell me when it is done.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Upper Route Planner data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run upper_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run upper_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run upper_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. upper_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: upper_list_drivers
tools.title: List drivers
tools.description: List the active drivers on the Upper team that owns the API token: id, name, email and phone. Use the ids with upper_assign_drivers and upper_share_route_to_drivers. GET /ext-get-drivers.

tools.name: upper_list_stops
tools.title: List stops
tools.description: List the team's stops in optimized order: address, coordinates, contact, time window, duration, status, route_id and custom ids. Pass route_id for one route (optionally scheduled=true/false); pass unscheduled=true (without route_id) for stops not on any route; with no filter all active stops are returned. Upper has no paging, so this tool pages locally: `limit` stops (default 100, max 500) starting at `offset`; the reply says if more remain (truncated, next_offset). GET /ext-get-stops.

route_id.description: Only the stops on this route.

scheduled.description: With route_id only: true = scheduled stops, false = unscheduled stops of that route.

unscheduled.description: Without route_id: true = unscheduled stops across all routes.

offset.description: Skip this many stops (use next_offset from the previous reply to read on).

tools.name: upper_get_optimization_status
tools.title: Get route optimization status
tools.description: Check whether a route is optimized: status is optimized, pending (still running) or not_optimized, plus the queue_id of the last job. Poll this after upper_optimize_route. GET /ext-optimization-status.

tools.name: upper_get_custom_fields
tools.title: Get stop custom fields
tools.description: The workspace's five stop custom-field slots (custom1 - custom5: type, label, enabled, required) and which are enabled. Needs the Custom fields feature in the Upper plan. GET /ext-get-custom-fields.

tools.name: upper_get_capacity_fields
tools.title: Get capacity fields
tools.description: The workspace's five capacity-field slots (capacity1 - capacity5: label, unit, enabled) used for load planning. GET /ext-get-capacity-fields.

tools.name: upper_create_route
tools.title: Create route
tools.description: WRITE: create a new, empty route (name, date, optimization preference, units, pickup sequencing, service time). Omitted settings fall back to the account's defaults. Returns the new route_id; add stops with upper_create_stop. Calling it twice creates two routes. POST /ext-create-route.

pickup_settings.description: When pickups are sequenced: auto, before or after the deliveries.

tools.name: upper_update_route
tools.title: Update route
tools.description: WRITE: change settings of an existing route (name, date, optimize_for, units, pickup_settings, service_time). Only the fields you pass change. POST /ext-update-route.

pickup_settings.description: When pickups are sequenced: auto, before or after.

tools.name: upper_create_stop
tools.title: Create stop
tools.description: WRITE: create a stop. The address is geocoded by Upper. Pass route_id to put it on a route (the route must not be active/in progress; an optimized route is flagged for re-optimization); omit it for an unscheduled stop. Calling it twice creates two stops. POST /ext-create-stop.

address.description: Street address of the stop (geocoded by Upper).

route_id.description: Route to attach the stop to; omit for an unscheduled stop.

state.description: State or region (overrides the geocoded value).

phone.description: Contact phone number; non-digits are stripped by Upper.

note.description: Free-text note shown to the driver.

start_time.description: Earliest service time (time window start), HH:MM or HH:MM:SS.

end_time.description: Latest service time (time window end), HH:MM or HH:MM:SS.

stop_duration.description: Service duration at the stop, in seconds.

stop_type.description: Stop type, for example Delivery or Pickup.

stop_priority.description: Stop priority, for example Normal, High, Urgent.

parcel_count.description: Number of parcels at the stop.

customer_system_id.description: Your own identifier for the stop (for cross-referencing).

custom_fields.description: Custom field values keyed by slot (custom1 - custom5). Only fields enabled in the workspace (and in the plan) are stored.

capacity_fields.description: Capacity values (integers) for load planning, keys capacity1 - capacity5.

tools.name: upper_update_stop
tools.title: Update stop
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing stop; only the fields you pass change. A new address is re-geocoded (city/state/zipcode you pass with it are ignored); city/state/zipcode apply only without an address. Passing route_id moves the stop to that route. Editing a stop on an optimized route flags the route for re-optimization; stops on an active route cannot be edited. POST /ext-update-stop.

route_id.description: Move the stop to this route.

city.description: City (only used when no address is passed).

state.description: State or region (only used when no address is passed).

zipcode.description: Postal code (only used when no address is passed).

phone.description: Contact phone number; non-digits are stripped by Upper.

note.description: Free-text note shown to the driver.

start_time.description: Earliest service time (time window start), HH:MM or HH:MM:SS.

end_time.description: Latest service time (time window end), HH:MM or HH:MM:SS.

stop_duration.description: Service duration at the stop, in seconds.

stop_type.description: Stop type, for example Delivery or Pickup.

stop_priority.description: Stop priority, for example Normal, High, Urgent.

parcel_count.description: Number of parcels at the stop.

customer_system_id.description: Your own identifier for the stop (for cross-referencing).

custom_fields.description: Custom field values keyed by slot (custom1 - custom5). Only fields enabled in the workspace (and in the plan) are stored.

capacity_fields.description: Capacity values (integers) for load planning, keys capacity1 - capacity5.

tools.name: upper_assign_drivers
tools.title: Assign drivers to a route
tools.description: WRITE: assign one or more drivers (ids from upper_list_drivers) to a route, replacing the route's drivers. Every id must be an active driver on the team. If the route was already optimized it is reset to unoptimized (needs_optimization: true), so run upper_optimize_route again. POST /ext-assign-drivers.

tools.name: upper_optimize_route
tools.title: Optimize route
tools.description: WRITE: start optimizing a route's stop order. The route needs at least one stop and one assigned driver (upper_assign_drivers). It runs asynchronously: this returns status pending and a queue_id, then poll upper_get_optimization_status. If a job is already running, that job is returned. POST /ext-optimize-route.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the optimization, for example America/New_York.

tools.name: upper_share_route_to_drivers
tools.title: Share route to drivers
tools.description: WRITE: push a route to the drivers' mobile app NOW, which sends each driver a notification. Without driver_ids the route's assigned drivers are used; with them, every id must be an active driver on the team. Sending twice notifies twice. Confirm with the user before calling. POST /ext-share-to-driver.

driver_ids.description: Drivers to notify (default: the route's assigned drivers).
